shots.scene: Madras, India, year 1952. A small south Indian railway station platform at hot noon, a black steam locomotive with third-class wooden coaches standing still, a few passengers in dhotis and sarees, station name board blank.

Madras, India, year 1952. Inside an old third-class railway coach with wooden bench seats, a large dark green steel trunk pushed under a seat, passengers nearby covering their noses with cloth and stepping back.

Madras, India, year 1952. A police constable in 1950s khaki uniform with shorts and a red-banded turban cap kneeling beside a large green steel trunk, lifting its lid, his face shocked, light glowing from inside the trunk, the inside of the trunk not visible.
A plain dark textured background with an old paper case file tied with red tape and a pair of round spectacles on a wooden desk.
Madras, India, year 1952. A busy 1950s Madras street corner with colonial red brick buildings, a tram, hand-pulled rickshaws, bullock carts and shop awnings in morning light.
Madras, India, year 1952. Inside a small old pen shop, a glass display case filled with rows of fountain pens and ink bottles, wooden shelves behind.
Madras, India, year 1952. A middle-aged south Indian salesman of about forty with a moustache, white shirt and dhoti, standing behind a pen shop counter, smiling, holding out a fountain pen.
Madras, India, year 1952. A sepia old photograph in a wooden frame of a young Indian soldier in a 1940s British Indian army khaki uniform standing straight.

Madras, India, year 1952. A young south Indian woman of twenty-two in a simple cotton saree with a long plait, standing at a pen shop counter looking at a fountain pen, the moustached salesman facing her.
Madras, India, year 1952. A simple 1950s Kerala style wedding, a young bride in a cream saree and a slim young groom in white shirt and mundu with garlands, a few relatives around.
Madras, India, year 1952. A small tiled-roof house with a wooden door on a quiet narrow street near the sea, a cemetery wall in the distance, evening light.
Madras, India, year 1952. Inside a dark 1950s cinema hall, light from the screen on a young couple sitting side by side, the woman speaking with her head lowered, the man's face tense and angry.
Madras, India, year 1952. Inside an old colonial police station, an inspector's wooden desk with registers and an inkpot, a constable writing a complaint in a big ledger.
Madras, India, year 1952. A tall south Indian police inspector in 1950s khaki uniform and peaked cap questioning two shop assistants inside a pen shop, a notebook in his hand.
Madras, India, year 1952. A small town hospital room, an elderly doctor in a white coat writing a report at a table, a closed green steel trunk on the floor in the corner.
A lonely unmarked earth mound with a small stone at the edge of a dry village field under a cloudy sky, palm trees far away.
Madras, India, year 1952. A police inspector sitting in a cane chair in the morning reading a folded newspaper with wide alert eyes, a steel tumbler of coffee on a side table.
Madras, India, year 1952. Two policemen in khaki forcing open a locked wooden door of a small tiled house, neighbours watching from a distance.
Madras, India, year 1952. An empty bare room of an old house with no furniture, a policeman's torch beam lighting a dull dark stain on a whitewashed wall.
Madras, India, year 1952. A thin hand-rickshaw puller in a vest and turban standing beside his rickshaw, pointing towards the sea while talking to a police inspector.

Madras, India, year 1952. A beach at dusk with fishing boats, seen from far away the dark silhouette of a man near the waves throwing a round cloth bundle into the sea, a rickshaw waiting on the sand.

Madras, India, year 1952. A big colonial railway station at night with gas lamps, a porter in a red shirt carrying a large green steel trunk on his head towards a waiting train, a man with a bandaged hand walking beside him seen from behind.
Madras, India, year 1952. A beach at evening, a police constable in khaki standing frozen in shock looking down at something hidden behind a small sand ridge near the waves, the object not visible.
Two old paper case files lying side by side on a wooden desk under a hanging lamp, a magnifying glass between them.
A police inspector standing in deep thought with a hand on his chin, large question marks drawn in the dark background around him.
A police inspector looking straight at the viewer and pointing a finger forward, serious questioning expression, plain dark background.
Madras, India, year 1952. A grand old colonial medical college building with arches and a clock tower, students in white walking in front, daylight.
Madras, India, year 1952. A 1950s laboratory, two Indian doctors in white coats and spectacles examining X-ray films held up against a light box.
A clean medical textbook style drawing of two neck vertebra bones fitting together like matching puzzle pieces, on aged paper.
A medical chart on aged paper showing the outline of a standing man next to a tall measuring scale, an open army service record book beside it.
A close view of a large magnifying glass held over two fingerprint cards placed side by side on a desk, the ridge patterns matching.
A wooden table with small labelled evidence items neatly arranged: a pair of green socks, a black waist thread, a cloth tag.
Madras, India, year 1952. A small servant boy seen from behind standing before a seated police inspector in an empty house, the inspector leaning forward listening.
Madras, India, year 1952. A small 1950s twin-propeller passenger aeroplane taking off from a simple airstrip, a few people waving.
Madras, India, year 1952. A 1950s Bombay street with chawl buildings and a double-decker bus, two policemen in khaki standing at the doorway of a house.
Madras, India, year 1952. A wooden table with a wrist watch, a sheathed knife and a fountain pen laid out, a beam of light falling on the fountain pen.
Madras, India, year 1952. The red Indo-Saracenic high court building with domes, a long queue of people in 1950s dress waiting outside its gates.
Madras, India, year 1952. Inside a 1950s courtroom, a lawyer in black gown and white bands arguing with a raised hand before a wooden jury box of twelve men.
Madras, India, year 1952. Inside a courtroom, a defence lawyer in a black gown speaking, behind him in the dock a young couple standing quietly with lowered eyes.
Madras, India, year 1952. A young woman in a plain saree sitting across a table from a police officer in a bare room, shaking her head in refusal, eyes lowered.
Madras, India, year 1952. An elderly Indian judge in black robes and spectacles seated on a high bench reading out a judgment from papers, courtroom silent.
A small roadside tea shop in Kerala among coconut palms, a couple seen from behind serving tea, green hills beyond.
A modern classroom of forensic science students in white coats, a teacher pointing at a drawing of neck bones on a blackboard.
A large brass weighing scale of justice on a dark background, one pan lower than the other, dramatic light.
A large old bungalow with a wide courtyard at night, moonlight, long shadows, one patch of the courtyard floor glowing faintly, mysterious mood.
